name: Spina Bifida-Hypospadias Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Spina Bifida-Hypospadias Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of spina bifida confirmed by clinical and imaging findings
Congenital hypospadias with abnormal urethral meatus location
Neurological abnormalities including lower limb weakness or sensory deficits
Additional urogenital anomalies such as cryptorchidism or chordee
MRI or ultrasound evidence of spinal cord malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both spina bifida and hypospadias confirmed clinically or by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may assist in differential diagnosis.

laboratory: Renal function tests may be abnormal in advanced cases
imaging: MRI demonstrating spinal cord malformations and tethered cord
Ultrasound or voiding cystourethrogram for urinary tract anomalies
X-rays showing vertebral defects and orthopedic deformities
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible sporadic or multifactorial inheritance
other: Clinical examination revealing open spinal defect and hypospadias

distinguishingFeatures: Closed spinal dysraphism without open neural tube defect
Sacral agenesis with lower limb abnormalities
Usually no hypospadias or open spinal defect

redFlags: Progressive lower limb weakness or paralysis
Urinary retention or incontinence indicating neurogenic bladder
Signs of increased intracranial pressure suggesting hydrocephalus
references: National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Spina Bifida
Smith DW, et al. Congenital malformations involving spinal dysraphism and hypospadias. Am J Med Genet. 1990.
